topics.topic: Whether allowed_preflight is a refusal or a successful transport-guard outcome
questions: Is `allowed_preflight` a refusal produced by the transport guard, or a successful transport outcome that must not be a member of `TransportGuardRefusal`?
Is `allowed_preflight` a successful transport-guard response, or is every `TransportGuardRefusal` member necessarily a refusal?
Is allowed_preflight actually a refusal with a refusal status, or is TransportGuardRefusal misnamed and intended to include successful transport-guard outcomes?

quotes: install_transport_guards: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST register exactly one FastAPI http middleware on the supplied application. For every request the middleware MUST evaluate the checks below in the order they are written, and the order is a pipeline rather than a choice between alternatives: each check either produces the response named for it and ends the request there, or leaves the request untouched for the next check to evaluate. A check that does not produce a response MUST NOT call the next handler, MUST NOT return, and MUST NOT cause any later check to be skipped; the next handler is called exactly once, after every check in the list has left the request unrefused. The status of each response a check produces is the status_code of the row of the imported TRANSPORT_GUARD_STATUSES constant selected by the = models.TransportGuardRefusal member named in parentheses. The checks are: derive a request id carrying no identity or credential material; reject the request (UNTRUSTED_HOST) when _host_allowed refuses the request host against the trusted_hosts field of the settings; answer an OPTIONS request carrying an Origin listed in the allowed_origins field of the settings with a preflight (ALLOWED_PREFLIGHT) echoing the requested method and headers plus Vary Origin, together with the allow-origin and allow-credentials headers every allowed-origin response carries, and reject an unlisted origin (UNLISTED_PREFLIGHT_ORIGIN); reject POST on the canonical viewer logout path, the imported VIEWER_LOGOUT_PATH constant, (LOGOUT_ORIGIN_MISMATCH) unless _normalized_origin of the request Origin equals _normalized_origin of the public_origin field of the settings; reject (OVERSIZED_BODY) when _body_within_limit refuses the declared Content-Length against the max_request_body_bytes field of the settings; reject (RATE_LIMITED) when _record_viewer_entry_attempt refuses a POST on the canonical viewer entry path, the imported VIEWER_ENTRY_PATH constant, keyed by _client_bucket_key, before any credential parsing or verification.
judgement.why: State 7 explicitly makes ALLOWED_PREFLIGHT the successful preflight response even though the enum carrying its status is named TransportGuardRefusal.

topics.topic: Whether supported-version identity includes the contract family
questions: Does a supported-version fact include the external contract it applies to, or is the same integer-valued row one identity across the snapshot and OCR contracts?

Is a supported version identified only by its integer, as the stated value identity implies, or by the pair of contract family and integer so that equal snapshot and OCR version numbers remain different facts?

quotes: _validate_snapshot_publication: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST accept only a snapshot contract version equal to the version of a row of the imported SUPPORTED_SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_VERSIONS constant, the currency the imported MONEY_CURRENCY constant names and R9 values, complete closed DTO fields, and project identity without consulting mutable PresuPro state.

create_expense_from_recognition: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST accept only confirmed complete normalized input whose contract_version equals the version of a row of the imported SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS constant, validate explicit allocations, apply R8 replay before mutation, and atomically insert one Expense plus one ExpenseDocument plus allocations and the expense-create member of = models.AuditAction audit.
judgement.why: State 7 validates snapshot and OCR versions against separate constants, so equal integers do not transfer support from one contract family to the other.

topics.topic: Whether capability membership requires exhaustive rows and what an absent pair means
questions: Must CAPABILITY_SET_MEMBERS contain exactly one row for every CapabilitySet–Capability pair, or may it contain only selected pairs; if a pair has no row, is membership false or unspecified?

quotes: The sets are data the generated guard reads: the data-provider constant `CAPABILITY_SET_MEMBERS` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10 version 2), a table keyed by `= models.CapabilitySet` and `= models.Capability` and total over both, in place of `rules.principal_capability_sets`. The administrator set is the operator set together with `administrator_additions`, an operation the notes of `_require_capability` state. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): values unchanged.
judgement.why: State 2 says the table is total over both closed key taxonomies, so an absent pair is not an alternative representation of false membership.

topics.topic: Whether data-provider tables normatively determine behavior or merely describe it
questions: Are the data-provider tables normative inputs that determine authorization, permitted status changes, audit classification, HTTP responses and command outcomes, or are they only non-behavioural descriptions of decisions made elsewhere?

quotes: The sets are data the generated guard reads: the data-provider constant `CAPABILITY_SET_MEMBERS` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10 version 2), a table keyed by `= models.CapabilitySet` and `= models.Capability` and total over both, in place of `rules.principal_capability_sets`. The administrator set is the operator set together with `administrator_additions`, an operation the notes of `_require_capability` state. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): values unchanged.

The staff and principal tables, which generated code reads, are the data-provider constants `STAFF_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` and `PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10 version 2: keyed by the pair of statuses, total, `allowed`). The viewer, grant and budget-version tables stay `rules.status_transitions`; no note reads them as data. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): values unchanged.

`rules.http_transport_policy` with its runtime settings (A30); the
deterministic HTTP router and the viewer cookie backend read it. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): the values the generated transport guard and runtime read are data-provider constants: `API_PREFIX`, `VIEWER_ENTRY_PATH`, `VIEWER_LOGOUT_PATH`, `NO_STORE_PATHS`, `NO_STORE_CACHE_CONTROL`, `SECURITY_HEADERS`, `TRANSPORT_LOG_LABELS`, `HEALTH_LIVE_PATH`, `HEALTH_READY_PATH`, `HEALTH_OK_STATUS`, and `TRANSPORT_GUARD_STATUSES`, the status of each refusal of the guard keyed by `= models.TransportGuardRefusal`. Their former leaves (`public_api_prefix`, `security_headers`, `browser_session.logout_path`, `health.liveness_path`, `health.readiness_path`) leave the policy; the cookie name and attributes stay, the viewer cookie backend reads them.
judgement.why: State 2 explicitly says generated authorization, status-transition, and transport code reads these constants; the State 1 statement means the data-placement change preserves existing behavior, not that the tables are non-normative.

topics.topic: Whether data-provider value-type members are release-defined or runtime-minted
questions: Are CapabilitySet, ImportAuditReason, TransportGuardRefusal and BootstrapCommandOutcome release-defined value types minted by SPEC_STANDARD from the data provider, or are their members runtime outcomes minted by the product actions that return them?

topics.topic: Whether principal-status transition rows are exhaustive and what an absent pair means
questions: For the principal type or types M42 governs, must PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS contain one row for every ordered status pair, or does omission itself mean disallowed?

quotes: The staff and principal tables, which generated code reads, are the data-provider constants `STAFF_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` and `PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10 version 2: keyed by the pair of statuses, total, `allowed`). The viewer, grant and budget-version tables stay `rules.status_transitions`; no note reads them as data. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): values unchanged.
judgement.why: State 2 requires PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS to be total over ordered status pairs, so omission is not the representation of a disallowed transition.

topics.topic: Whether staff-status transition rows are exhaustive and what an absent pair means
questions: Must STAFF_STATUS_TRANSITIONS contain exactly one row for every ordered StaffStatus pair, or may disallowed transitions be omitted; what fact does an absent pair represent?

quotes: The staff and principal tables, which generated code reads, are the data-provider constants `STAFF_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` and `PRINCIPAL_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10 version 2: keyed by the pair of statuses, total, `allowed`). The viewer, grant and budget-version tables stay `rules.status_transitions`; no note reads them as data. Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): values unchanged.
judgement.why: State 2 requires STAFF_STATUS_TRANSITIONS to be total over ordered status pairs, so every pair has an explicit allowed value.

topics.topic: Whether supported contract versions use a closed enumeration or unrestricted integers
questions: Must a supported contract-version key be promoted to a closed enumeration, or does M43 intentionally retain an unrestricted integer field?

quotes: The accepted versions are the data-provider constants `SUPPORTED_SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_VERSIONS` and `SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS` (SPEC_STANDARD 6.10, a `record_tuple` of `SupportedContractVersion` rows, because 6.10 has no integer tuple). Data placement 2026-11-08 (owner: the specification rebuilt by SPEC_STANDARD; SOURCE.md "Data placement"): in place of `rules.supported_external_contract_versions`, values unchanged.
judgement.why: State 2 explicitly represents supported versions as record tuples of SupportedContractVersion rows rather than promoting each integer version to an enum member.
